subtopics.label: Unusually Low Winter Ice Cover
subtopics.attitude: Observational and Concerned about Low Ice Cover
subtopics.summary: Discussion in this cluster focuses on the significantly low ice cover observed on the Great Lakes during the winter season. Reports indicate the lakes were only 7% ice-covered as of February 13th, which is significantly below the expected 35-40% for that time of year [109883990352883012]. Another report states the Great Lakes winter ice cover averaged just 5.9% [111937295945084150]. Commenters express concern that this low ice cover will be a "huge problem," even noting similar local issues with lake levels [111964992905405845].

key_quotes.quote: only 7% ice-covered, which is significantly below the 35-40% ice cover that is expected
key_quotes.note: This quote quantifies the unusually low ice cover and highlights the deviation from typical expectations for the season.

key_quotes.quote: Great Lakes Winter Ice Cover Averaging Just 5.9%: NOAA
key_quotes.note: This provides a concise, official statistic regarding the overall low average ice cover for the winter.

key_quotes.quote: The ice cover on the lakes is going to be a huge problem.
key_quotes.note: This quote directly expresses the sentiment of concern and potential negative impacts associated with the observed low ice cover.

subtopics.label: Great Lakes Winter Storm Forecasts
subtopics.summary: This cluster focuses on forecasts for significant late-season and mid-season winter storms impacting the Upper Midwest and Great Lakes region [116331872300163982, 116223846039744801]. Discussions highlight warnings for heavy ice, sleet, snow, and potentially record snowfall, which are expected to create hazardous driving conditions due to reduced visibility from snow squalls [116331872300163982, 116223846039744801, 113787218854837950].
